The last syllable had not yet faded before a right fist shot out like lightning — aimed directly, furiously, at that insufferable face.

The figure across from him shifted one step sideways. That iron fist grazed the side of his neck and fell into empty air.

"The young master's skill is impressive indeed." The words came out lightly and without effort, and a finger moved with the same lightness, tapping toward the fist near his neck.

He had seen it clearly, dodged swiftly, and gotten away clearly — and yet, when he looked down at his right hand, he found it unharmed on the surface. But the whole palm burned with a deep, drilling pain.

He raised his head and looked at the figure across from him.

Just standing there. Jade fan moving gently. The smile exactly as before. Utterly relaxed and free. But in this moment, Yuwen Feng — for all his sky-high arrogance — knew with perfect clarity: the person across from him was terrifying. Perhaps to everyone else it looked like nothing but a simple, direct punch. But in truth, that punch had been thrown with ten parts of his fury, ten parts of his full power, at the fastest speed he could muster — because he had made up his mind with that punch to shatter that hateful face.

And yet the person across from him... that martial skill was perhaps like those jade-green eyes: something seen nowhere else in all the world.

Shen'er — heaven is vast and full of people beyond your knowledge. You cannot know how deep or wide the jianghu runs or how many skilled fighters lie hidden within it. You must remember: know yourself. Never push against what you cannot change. His grandfather's earnest, gentle words sounded suddenly in his ear.

But I... I am Yuwen Feng! And Yuwen Feng does not bow to his enemies!

"The Seventh Young Master is truly as his name suggests." Yuwen Feng steadied his breath, fixed his gaze on Lan Qi, and slowly raised both palms.

"Trouble." From their distant perch, Yuwen Luo took one look at Yuwen Feng's posture and felt his stomach sink.

Ning Lang had been watching the fight intently, but hearing this, he turned to look at Yuwen Luo. "What is it?"

"Could my older brother truly be finished here?" Yuwen Luo's grip tightened on the brush.

Ning Lang heard this and his own heart clenched. He turned back to look at the two figures facing off in the courtyard.

Yuwen Feng stood watching Lan Qi in silence, both palms held horizontally before his chest, no shift of expression, no movement — calm, composed, radiating the bearing of a true master. But what sent a deeper chill through those watching was the faint crimson at the center of each of his palms.

"The Crimson Heart Palm! He's actually using it!" Yuwen Luo sucked in a sharp breath at the sight.

Ning Lang's own expression changed. Simple as he might be when it came to people and social situations, he understood the martial path deeply — he had been born into an illustrious family and his parents and master were each masters of their generation. The Yuwen family's weapon of renown was the Scarlet Dragon Whip — but the technique that made the Yuwen family truly feared, never lightly deployed and never passed to outsiders, was the "Crimson Heart Palm."

Crimson Heart, No Regrets — that was how the jianghu had described the Crimson Heart Palm for a hundred years.

Once the Crimson Heart Palm is used, there is no turning back.

In every generation, the Yuwen family selected disciples of exceptional talent to inherit the technique — but over the span of more than a hundred years, only two had ever achieved mastery. All the others had barely reached what could be called half-cultivation. Yet even half-cultivation of the Crimson Heart Palm was enough to carry the Yuwen family through a century of jianghu conflicts, standing firm as one of the great clans. And now, Yuwen Feng had brought out this technique — a technique he had never deployed since first entering the jianghu. Because so few had ever mastered it, no one in the current jianghu had ever actually witnessed it firsthand. According to the stories passed down through the generations: when the Crimson Heart Palm is first being cultivated, both palms run deep red. As progress is made, the redness recedes. When mastery is complete, only a single point of crimson remains — and that is the origin of the palm's name. At this moment, the red at Yuwen Feng's palms covered an area of roughly an inch — which meant he had reached approximately half the cultivation.

"No wonder the elders placed such great hopes in my older brother. He truly is the finest of the Yuwen family." Yuwen Luo murmured.

"What will he do against it?" What Ning Lang worried about was someone else entirely.

Even the ever-smiling Lan Qi let a flicker of genuine surprise enter his eyes as he looked at Yuwen Feng. The casual dismissiveness in his gaze disappeared.

"The young master's family learning runs very deep indeed."

The final syllable of "indeed" had not yet fully left his lips when those jade-green eyes blazed — the purple-clad figure moved without warning, and before any person in the courtyard had time to register it, a single finger pierced the air and shot directly for Yuwen Feng.

The sharpness of a jade sword splitting the wind in that single finger!

The swiftness of lightning and fire in that single finger!

And in that single finger — a fatal, soul-stealing wickedness!

And in that single finger — a beguiling force that could bewitch ten thousand spirits!

In the courtyard, hearts seized and minds reeled. In the wake of that single instant of shock, bodies instinctively stumbled back — as though that finger were aimed at each of them.

In that moment, Ming Er's eyes — usually soft and shrouded as mist — flashed cold and sharp, and the hand resting on the chair arm clenched into a fist.

Yuwen Feng looked up and saw that heart-stopping finger. In that single instant his soul gave a jolt — but his body had already reacted before his mind could, both palms striking out, feet shifting. And yet in that same instant, a pain struck his throat, and he could no longer move at all.

The courtyard fell into total silence.

Every person stared.

That one finger — long and pale and beautiful — rested its tip at Yuwen Feng's throat, poised like a sword at the neck.

Yuwen Feng's palms had only reached halfway.

Winner and loser in a single instant. The contest was decided.

Yuwen Luo and Ning Lang stared at each other, then exhaled — long and difficult — before one of them asked: "Was that a sneak attack?"

That was the question every hero in the courtyard wanted to ask.

Too fast! Even a sneak attack isn't that fast! Giving no warning at all before striking is no act of a hero!

"Of course not!" Ning Lang answered immediately.

The words rang out louder than he intended in the stillness of the courtyard, and every gaze swung toward this corner, including Lan Qi's — who, spotting Ning Lang, let that look of amused interest surface once more in his eyes.

"My older brother had already moved first." Ning Lang said this much more quietly — so quietly that even Yuwen Luo, sitting right beside him, had to strain to catch it.

"I concede." Lan Qi's jade fan opened. He withdrew his finger.

Yuwen Feng stared hard at Lan Qi — the eyes carrying fury, hatred, shame, indignation, and beneath it all, a thin stratum of shock. After a long moment, he said without any expression: "Many thanks to the Seventh Young Master for showing mercy." Then he turned, bowed once toward the small central pavilion, and said: "Your nephew has been defeated. I will take my leave." Without waiting for Qiu Changtian or Nan Wofeng to respond, he turned and walked. In moments his figure had disappeared through the gate.

Qiu Changtian glanced at Qiu Zang, who understood immediately and hurried after him.

The courtyard, which had by now come back to its senses, followed Yuwen Feng's swift retreating figure until it vanished, then turned back to look at the man standing at the center of the ring, jade fan swaying at ease. Every last person fell into silent thought.

Everyone had seen Yuwen Feng's skill with their own eyes — an absolute first-rate fighter. Yet a man of that caliber had been beaten by a single move, a single finger, in a single instant. The skill of this man...

It was unnervingly high.

"Might any of the gathered heroes be willing to offer their instruction?" Lan Qi's gaze swept a slow arc across the courtyard.

No one spoke.

Lan Qi smiled in great satisfaction. His gaze drifted to the small pavilion and settled, light and easy, on Ming Er. "Second Young Master — shall we play a little?"

Ming Er rose with a smile, his misty eyes meeting Lan Qi's. Azure robes stirred and the figure was already at the pavilion's edge.

"How could I not accept the Seventh Young Master's invitation?"

"The Ming family's 'Infinite Space Fingers' are unrivaled in the world — this one has longed to see them for some time."

One side: Lan Qi, jade fan swaying lightly, smile wicked and faint.

"I have heard said that the Seventh Young Master has never been seen to use the Lan family's own techniques, and that his true martial lineage remains a mystery. I, too, find myself most curious."

The other side: Ming Er, steady as a green lotus in a breeze, his smile like spring wind over water.

Both trained their volleys on each other with precision — and the courtyard erupted.

The Second Young Master of the Ming family, the Seventh Young Master of the Lan family, and Lie Chifeng of the Lie family were known together as the "Three Young Masters of the Martial World" — the three most distinguished members of the martial world's younger generation. Lie Chifeng, besotted with his blade, went everywhere looking for skilled fighters to challenge and was known to many in the jianghu, and there were those who had seen his martial skill and his bladework firsthand. But Ming Er and Lan Qi had each burst onto the scene as a young prodigy, dazzling the world before seeming to vanish like a brilliant but brief flash of light — and had barely shown themselves in public since, though tales of their deeds continued to circulate. Only in the last two years had they moved more openly in the jianghu. Yet even now neither seemed particularly inclined to act, and very few had ever witnessed their skills directly. Those rare few who had been fortunate enough to observe them were left awestruck.

And so the martial abilities of these two had become one of the ten great mysteries of the jianghu.

And now, at this place, these two were about to settle things between them. How could that fail to stir curiosity and excitement in every person present?

In an instant, every eye in the courtyard was fixed and fully alert.

chapters.title: Chapter Four: Born Rivals (Part Two)
chapters.content:
When the highest masters do battle, some are as ferocious as tigers, their force enough to alter heaven and earth, the fighting growing so intense that the skies may seem to change color. Others weave a hundred — a thousand — endlessly varied techniques, fighting for days and nights without a decisive outcome. Others still achieve a state of perfect, motionless stillness — purged of all distraction, holding that stillness for a day and a night — all in preparation for a single, decisive strike.

But no matter the style, every contest of such men inevitably culminates in a vast, surging, blood-stirring finale.

Nothing like what was happening now.

"Why not allow the Second Young Master to demonstrate the 'Infinite Space Fingers?' If this one could witness a supreme martial technique with his own eyes, then losing outright would be no dishonor." Lan Qi raised his hand in a bow that was the very picture of stately grace — the name "jade demon" seemed hardly misplaced.

"I have heard it said that the Seventh Young Master is a genius who has mastered the techniques of every school, yet no one has ever seen what his true martial art actually is. If Ming Er could witness it, that would be the highest of honors." Ming Huayan returned the bow with the poise of an immortal descended from the heavens.

"If the Second Young Master were willing to offer a pointer or two, this one would be endlessly enriched."

"The Seventh Young Master speaks too modestly — it is Ming Er who ought to seek guidance from him."

"This one's shortcomings are no match for the Second Young Master."

"Ming Er's ignorance could not compare to the Seventh Young Master's learning."

...

Back and forth the two men deferred to each other. The onlookers grew nearly unbearable with impatience. Lan Qi had been so insufferably arrogant just moments ago — why, the moment he faced Ming Er, had he turned into this picture of humble courtesy? Did he truly know he was outmatched? Yet looking at his expression, where was the slightest sign of apprehension? Then why all this endless talk? If you are going to fight, just fight! And that Second Young Master of the Ming family, for all his immortal serenity — how could he be this indecisive!

"Mm!"

"Hmph!"

"Ahem!"

From every corner of the courtyard came a scattered chorus of frustrated breaths and sighs, and the patience of the onlookers was wearing very thin. Yuwen Luo's brush hand had broken into a sweat, his eyes riveted to both men, terrified of missing some once-in-a-thousand-years technique or stroke of genius — but those two were still exchanging pleasantries back and forth. He wanted nothing more than to give each of them a shove.

The only ones in the entire courtyard who remained perfectly composed were Qiu Changtian and Nan Wofeng.

"If we fight move for move, it might take days to reach a conclusion."

"Neither of us would tire — but the others would have a very long wait."

"The Qiu family's young mistress laid out this courtyard with exceptional care and feeling. I have not the heart to destroy it."

"This courtyard is exquisite as a painting. To damage it would be to burn the lute and boil the crane."

"The Second Young Master and I truly think alike. Might you have a solution that would spare us this one act of vulgarity?"

"If the Seventh Young Master frames it that way, you must already have thought of something — why ask me?"

"Then..."

The two looked at each other. They smiled.

Just move, just fight! Every spectator wanted to roar it aloud — but dared not, given who they were facing.

"We will not step beyond this two-zhang space."

"We will not move our attacks beyond each other."

Two clean, simple sentences, spoken quietly — and then, without warning, the courtyard seemed to blur. Purple motion, blue shift. In an instant, all that could be made out was a swirl of purple and blue — impossible to see who was where.

"One quarter-hour as the limit."

These words came from both at the same time — yet already the two were indistinguishable. All one could know was: purple sleeves billowing like storm clouds blotting out the sun — that was Lan Qi. Blue robes shifting as though the thinnest mist had drifted across the sky — that was Ming Er. Feet moving with the speed of lightning and arrows, bodies flashing with the agility of dragons and phoenixes, attack and technique as vast and boundless as sky and sea...

The sun stood high and clear overhead. Now and then, a clean breeze.

Though no one could make out the details, one could still half-sense: those two figures moved with a lightness and ease that seemed almost playful.

And yet, in that moment, cold sweat broke out across every forehead in the courtyard. Not a single eye could be pulled away.

No one dared approach that two-zhang space. No one dared draw near those two moving shadows.

A formless pressure. A wordless terror.

Ning Lang held his breath. Yuwen Luo's brush lay still, his eyes wide and unblinking. Hua Qinghe and Mei Hongming watched with composed gravity, fists tight. Qiu Changtian and Nan Wofeng observed in perfectly still concentration.

"The quarter-hour is nearly up." Lan Qi's voice, touched with a smile, drifted out.

"Then this will be the last." Ming Er's voice, warm and untroubled.

Purple shadow like a flowing wind. Azure robe like a drifting leaf. Coming close — then parting — and then the wind went still and the leaf ceased to move. Both figures stood where they had started, composed and untouched.

A long exhale moved through the courtyard. The tightness in every chest released at last, and a question arose: who had won?

As though to answer the question, two clear, crisp sounds rang out — like something snapping — and then two light, musical notes as two jade hairpins fell to the ground, each broken cleanly in two. Then, slowly, two hair crowns — one jade, one gold — began to slide downward, and, freed from their bindings, two cascades of long hair spilled outward and fell loose.

And in that instant, every person present was struck still.

Yuwen Luo stared until his eyes could barely focus. After a long moment he said to himself, in a faint and wondering murmur: "No wonder...no wonder the jianghu says even Qiu Hengbo and Hua Fushu don't qualify as the first beauty. There really is something to that."

"Then who does?" Back to his senses, Ning Lang asked.

"Can you not see for yourself?" Yuwen Luo still could not pull his eyes from Lan Qi.

Ning Lang opened his mouth, then let his gaze fall back on Lan Qi, and said blankly: "He is a man."

Yuwen Luo's lips moved. In the end, he held back what he was going to say. After all, it was only a rumor.

The Ming family's "Infinite Space Fingers." Lan Qi's true martial art. Neither had been revealed. Both of their hairpins had been broken, both hair crowns had fallen, and the bout had ended without a winner — but no one cared about that anymore.

Both had their hair loose. And yet the two figures were entirely different.

Azure-robed, standing tall and free in the breeze — that was the otherworldly serenity of the Banished Immortal.

Purple-clad, robes billowing, hair of dark ink half-concealing the face — that was the sinister enchantment of the Jade Demon.

When the eyes rested on Ming Er, the heart filled with reverence and admiration. But when the eyes fell on Lan Qi, something trembled and sank within every soul in the courtyard.

In that moment, every person present — man and woman alike — could not look away, and the rumor that had circulated in the jianghu for so long rose unbidden to the surface of every mind.

While the crowd was still rapt in that daze, a manor guard appeared and made his way quickly through the courtyard to the small central pavilion.

"Steward, there is someone outside the gate claiming to be from Shouling Palace on Ying Mountain, requesting an audience."

"Hmm?" Qiu Changtian rose in surprise. "You say a person from Shouling Palace?"

"Yes. The person says he is from Shouling Palace and has come here under orders."

"Show him in at once." Qiu Changtian said quickly.

At this point, not only Qiu Changtian but every other person present felt a deep and puzzled bewilderment. Everyone knew that the people of Shouling Palace concerned themselves only with guarding the Lanyin and Biyue — in over a hundred years they had never once set foot beyond Ying Mountain, never once involved themselves in jianghu affairs. And now, they had sent someone to Longsky Manor. What could this be about? No one was naive enough to assume the man had come to take part in the day's gathering. No matter how broad Qiu Changtian's reputation in the martial world, to the people of Shouling Palace it would carry no weight at all.

Lan Qi and Ming Er exchanged a glance, then together walked back to the small central pavilion.

A man in white crossed the courtyard, walked to Qiu Changtian, and bowed. He did not waste words on pleasantries — he simply reached into his robes and withdrew a letter. "On orders from the Palace Master, I am here to deliver this letter to Senior Qiu."

Qiu Changtian accepted it.

"The letter has been delivered. I will take my leave." The man in white bowed once more, turned, and made to go.

"Please, wait a moment." Qiu Changtian quickly tried to keep him. "You have come a long way — please rest here a while."

The man in white stopped, turned, and looked at Qiu Changtian without expression. "I am only here to deliver a letter. I know nothing more than that. The steward need only read the letter to understand the Palace Master's intent. I must return and report. I thank Senior Qiu for his kindness. Farewell." With that, he did not linger, and departed with long, quick strides.

The onlookers watched in some disbelief as he turned down an invitation that most people in the jianghu would beg for — and found themselves, for some reason, unable to speak a word of reproach when they saw the man's face and bearing. They simply stood and watched him go.

"One wonders what could bring Shouling Palace to break a century of precedent and send a letter to Longsky Manor," said Nan Wofeng, stepping from the pavilion with a thoughtful crease between his brows, looking toward the letter in Qiu Changtian's hand.

"Indeed." Qiu Changtian looked down at it. He had hoped to keep the messenger and learn more, but the man had refused with a finality that left no room for further persuasion. "Perhaps the letter holds the answer."

These words sent every pair of eyes in the courtyard converging on the letter in Qiu Changtian's hand. Everyone was desperate to know. With the Lanyin Biyue just returned to Ying Mountain and a new lord of the martial world about to be chosen — why, at this of all times, would Shouling Palace be sending a letter to Qiu Changtian? Questions hung in every heart.

Qiu Changtian had initially planned to wait until after the gathering was over and read it in private — but now, looking at the expectant eyes around him, he reconsidered briefly and then smiled. "Perhaps I should read it here and now. If it is good news, let the assembled heroes share in the joy."

With that, he broke the seal and opened the letter on the spot.

Every person in the courtyard knew they could not see the letter itself, and yet still craned their necks, darting their eyes from the paper to Qiu Changtian's face — and what they saw made every heart seize with sudden dread: the color drained from Qiu Changtian's face.

"Long Tian?" Nan Wofeng asked with concern, alarmed by what he saw.

Qiu Changtian raised his eyes and met Nan Wofeng's gaze — his own full of shock and disbelief. The letter trembled in his hand as he held it toward Nan Wofeng: "Shouling Palace says... the Lanyin Biyue has been stolen."

"What?!"

"That's impossible!"

"Is it true?"

"No one has ever managed to take anything from Shouling Palace in all these years — surely this is not real?"

"If the Lanyin Biyue is gone, will the Grand Assembly on Ying Mountain still proceed?"

"Without the Lanyin Order, how is a new lord of the martial world to be chosen?"

...

The courtyard erupted. The matter of the bouts was entirely forgotten. The Celestial Silk Robe was precious, but what could it compare to the symbol of the supreme ruler of the martial world?

Qiu Changtian looked around at the scene, exchanged a glance with Nan Wofeng, and signaled to the manor servant who was holding the Celestial Silk Robe to step back.

"Everyone!" Qiu Changtian's voice rose above the clamor.

The crowd quieted and looked toward him.

"The theft of the Lanyin Biyue from Ying Mountain is a matter that concerns every person in the entire martial world. Shouling Palace has already sent word to both the White Path and the Black Path, calling all to gather on Ying Mountain on the tenth day of the eighth month. I expect the palace will have something to say at that time. The Lanyin Biyue is not a trivial matter — it touches the peace and safety of the entire jianghu. Today's gathering at Longsky must be cut short. I ask each of the gathered heroes to make their way home, gather what information you can, alert your sects and families, and think about any leads that might help in recovering the Lanyin Biyue. Let us all meet again on Ying Mountain on the tenth day of the eighth month and discuss this together. What say you all?"

The courtyard fell briefly quiet, then voices began rising in agreement — more or less aligned with what Qiu Changtian had proposed.

Qiu Changtian looked at the sun and said: "It is nearly noon. Please allow Longsky Manor to offer the gathered heroes a midday meal. I have only a simple meal and thin wine to offer — I hope the gathered heroes will not find it beneath them."

"Steward, please do not say such things — we have already imposed greatly on you."

"We are most grateful for the steward's hospitality."

Many voices rose in agreement and thanks.

Qiu Changtian instructed the servants to have tables set out in the courtyard.

Over on their side, Ning Lang could no longer sit still, and kept craning his neck to look toward the small central pavilion.

Yuwen Luo watched his manner and couldn't help but smile. Ning Lang caught him smiling and felt a little embarrassed. "After we eat, everyone will be leaving... and I still haven't..."

"You're afraid you'll miss your chance, and after today you'll never get to see him again, so you want to go make his acquaintance?" Yuwen Luo finished it for him. "Well, I want to meet both of them too. Come on — you have to know when to seize the moment." He grabbed Ning Lang and headed for the small central pavilion.

Arriving there, Qiu Changtian saw Yuwen Luo pulling Ning Lang over and quickly made the introductions: "These two are Yuwen Luo of the Yuwen family and Ning Lang of the Ning family — you may not have met them before, Second Young Master and Seventh Young Master."

Ming Er and Lan Qi both turned and smiled in greeting.

Seen from a distance, the two had already been incomparably striking — but up close, their bearing and presence struck even harder. Yuwen Luo's heart was racing with excitement. He was just thinking about how to start a conversation when Ning Lang, unexpectedly, spoke first.

"Sev...Seventh Young Master, you...you..." He had managed to begin, but words failed him completely.

"Hmm?" Lan Qi looked at him, jade-green eyes full of amusement.

"I...I..." Ning Lang felt heat flood his face, his heart pounding wildly. The words refused to come.

Yuwen Luo had no patience for his brother's performance, and gave his shoulder a clap. "A man of the jianghu speaks his mind clearly and loudly. All this stammering — do you want people to laugh at you?"

"You..." Ning Lang opened his mouth, got halfway through something, and swallowed it back.

"What is it you want to say?" Those jade-green eyes, deep and still, seemed to carry both encouragement and something subtly enthralling.

"You...you..."

"Ahem! If you have something to say, say it directly!" Yuwen Luo gave him a shake.

"Do you know Lan Canyin?"

The words burst out of him unexpectedly loud, ringing across the entire courtyard. Everyone looked toward the pavilion — and a moment later, "Ha ha ha ha..." Laughter broke out in waves.

Yuwen Luo buried his face in his hands, deeply regretting ever having sworn brotherhood with someone this simple-minded.

The others in the pavilion also froze for a brief, blank moment before breaking into low laughter — only Ning Lang still stood there obliviously, not understanding why everyone was laughing.

"You don't know the Seventh Young Master of the Lan family's given name?" Yuwen Luo — out of loyalty to his sworn brother — couldn't help but offer the rescue.

"Isn't it just Lan Qi?" Ning Lang answered. Wasn't that what everyone called him?

"Good heavens..." Yuwen Luo covered his face again, then raised his voice to Ning Lang: "Qi is his position in the Lan family. His actual name is Lan Canyin!"

"What?" Ning Lang froze — then cried out: "That's impossible!"

"Why is it impossible?" Yuwen Luo showed his little pointed canine teeth in a wide stare, looking very much like he wanted to leap over and take a bite. "The Seventh Young Master of the Lan family, Lan Canyin — who in the martial world doesn't know that!"

"How is that possible?" Ning Lang still couldn't believe it. He turned to look at Lan Qi, who was fanning himself with casual ease, the picture of unhurried elegance. "You...you are Lan Canyin?"

"Lan Qi is indeed called Lan Canyin — is there something wrong with that?" Lan Qi, looking genuinely puzzled, turned his face to Ning Lang. Yet in the depths of those jade-green eyes something mysterious and unreadable lurked.

"You are Lan Canyin? You are Lan Canyin!" As though struck by lightning, Ning Lang raised his hand and pointed, his somewhat dark face now drained of color. His expression was one of sheer panic and disbelief. "This...how is this possible...you...I..."

"What is it?" Yuwen Luo took one look at the devastated expression on his little brother's face and quickly caught him by the arm.

"You...you...how can you be a man?" The shock on Ning Lang's face had crumbled into something close to a funeral expression. "How can you possibly be a man?!"

A gleam of strange light passed through Lan Qi's jade-green eyes. He rose and walked toward Ning Lang. Ning Lang stepped back involuntarily.

Lan Qi opened both hands, spreading them in a gesture of helplessness. "This one is indeed a man. Is that very unsatisfactory?"

Ning Lang looked at the person before him — purple robes, jade-green eyes, beauty without parallel — and yet... a man. He felt five different flavors warring in his chest, too tangled to sort out, and said, low and murmuring: "I...I am Ning Lang of Lan Province." That ought to tell you everything.

"Ning Lang...Ning Lang of Lan Province..." Lan Qi repeated the name twice, voice low and gentle. Ning Lang felt, for no reason he could explain, a strange sensation stir somewhere inside him — but the moment he thought about the reality before him, it dissolved into nothing but a chest full of bitterness.

"Oh..." Lan Qi suddenly brightened with realization. "This one remembers now!" He turned to look at Ning Lang, those jade-green eyes shining brightly. Ning Lang felt a bone-deep shudder — and as Lan Qi walked still closer, Ning Lang backed away involuntarily, stumbled back out of the small pavilion, and found himself standing at the base of the steps.

Separated now by several steps, Lan Qi looked down at Ning Lang from the height of the pavilion — jade-green eyes flowing, an utterly beguiling smile, full of delight.

"So you are this one's..."

The voice paused here, just for a moment. The entire courtyard strained to hear. Ning Lang's heart lurched with panic, and he desperately wanted to stop whatever was coming next — but something seemed to have sealed his throat.

"...promised one!"

With these clear, bright words settling into the air, the courtyard erupted in the sound of tables and chairs hitting the ground.

"What...did you say..." Yuwen Luo's eyes had gone round as eggs; his tongue had knotted.

Qiu Changtian and Nan Wofeng wore expressions of complete stupefaction, their dignified elder's bearing knocked somewhat askew. The eldest son of the Hua family's warm and gracious smile went rigid. Even Mei Hongming snapped his head up, all signs of contemplation gone.

Only Ming Er's brow gave a slight movement, and those misty eyes turned toward Ning Lang with a look of faint, gentle sympathy.

Had they just heard that correctly?

That was the question every hero in the courtyard was silently asking themselves.

Everyone had heard of betrothed wives and betrothed husbands — but "promised one" between two men? No, no — they must have misheard. They must have misheard!

Before they had quite finished convincing themselves of this, another sentence arrived.

"Ning Lang — shall we be married today?"

"Thud." Someone fell.

"You...I...we're both men — a marriage contract between us can't possibly count..." Ning Lang stumbled over his words trying to say this, and Lan Qi cut him off.

"Are you saying you want to dissolve our marriage contract?" Lan Qi's face transformed into a picture of disbelief and injury. "Are you going to abandon me? Are you about to become a person who breaks his word and dishonors his promises? Or have you found someone else? I may be of little worth, but all these years I have kept myself pure and waited faithfully for you. And now you treat me this way. Where is your conscience?"

Kept himself pure.

Several people in the courtyard thought, at the same time, of a particular collection of stories that had spread through the jianghu.

Some could only inwardly sigh: Jade Demon — Jade Demon — this name was clearly not given in error. A proper, upright person would never, ever ask such things.

"I...I am not..." Ning Lang had been pummeled by this barrage of questions into a daze.

"This one knew you were not." Lan Qi gave a satisfied nod, and those jade-green eyes narrowed just slightly, rippling with a gentle light. "Tell me — when shall we be married?"

"Married?" Ning Lang's breath caught in his throat.

"Yes." Lan Qi's eyes blinked lightly. "We are both well past the age for it, and now that we have finally met — of course we should be married as soon as possible."

That breath stuck in Ning Lang's throat was unbearable. He opened his mouth and let it out, along with the one thought in his heart: "Two men cannot be married!"

"Why not?" Lan Qi raised one brow. "Which law of the dynasty says men may not marry men?"

There was no law that explicitly said so, but still—

"It has never been done in all of history!" Ning Lang's face was burning red.

"Then we shall be the first in all of history." Lan Qi smiled, completely unbothered.

"You...you..." Ning Lang had no answer, and could only stare at Lan Qi, his mind one great tangle.

"Ning Lang, what if we were married today? With so many friends from the jianghu already here, we wouldn't even have to send invitations." Lan Qi offered the suggestion with perfect ease.

"Married today?" By now Ning Lang's brain was not merely tangled — it was spinning.

"Yes. We jianghu people need not stand on such formalities. Senior Qiu and Senior Nan are both on good terms with our respective families — as our elders, they can officiate. We will hold the ceremony right here at Longsky Manor."

As Lan Qi spoke, he descended the steps and reached out to take Ning Lang's hand. Ning Lang sprang back as though burned, and either he jumped too forcefully or his footing gave way — "bang!" — and he toppled straight onto the ground.

The assembled crowd, which had been caught between laughter and bewilderment, erupted into helpless laughter at the sight of him on the ground. Some pounded the table, some leaned on each other, some pointed at Ning Lang, some clutched their stomachs, some wiped the corners of their eyes...

Ning Lang looked at Lan Qi advancing step by step toward him, then looked at the courtyard full of delighted, jeering faces. Panic and shame combined. His eyes grew hot, and throwing all dignity aside, he shouted: "Big Brother!"

"Ah?" Yuwen Luo had been so startled he had momentarily left his own body, but this one panicked shout brought him back. He hurried over and helped Ning Lang up. "Get up — this marriage matter, this...hmm...well..." He "well'd" and "hmm'd" for a while without producing anything useful, then turned to face Lan Qi, took in the courtyard full of amused heroes, and found himself completely at a loss. He shifted his appeal to Qiu Changtian and Nan Wofeng — surely, as elders and old family friends, they were obliged to say something?

Qiu Changtian and Nan Wofeng looked at each other. The matter of a marriage contract between the Lan and Ning families was entirely new to them, but judging from Ning Lang's reaction, the contract evidently did exist — and yet...how could a marriage contract have been made between two boys? Had they perhaps been betrothed before birth and both turned out to be boys? But in terms of age, Lan Qi seemed to be two or three years older than Ning Lang, so the "betrothed before birth" theory didn't hold either. What could it be, then... they were still puzzling over this when Lan Qi spoke again.

"To think of all these years of longing and waiting, and yet you shrink from me as from a tiger... ah..." One long, lingering sigh, and the whole courtyard darkened in sympathy.

"That's not it...I...I..." Ning Lang looked at Lan Qi's sorrowful expression and felt panic grip him immediately.

"Ah..." Another sigh, and those jade-green eyes dimmed. A glance at Ning Lang — then the figure turned and walked away. A white ribbon bound the long hair from crown to tip, a curtain of ink-dark strands falling to cover the entire back, and against all that black the retreating figure looked overwhelmingly, aching, lonely.

Ning Lang felt something warm surge up in his chest, and before he could think the words came out: "I didn't! Don't be sad!"

Lan Qi stopped. The figure behind him seemed to tremble slightly.

Ning Lang shifted his feet and moved a little closer. "Don't be sad. This marriage contract matter... well... we... hmm..." Faltering and stumbling, each word a struggle — and then he noticed that the back of the figure ahead of him was shaking rather violently. He could only assume the man was overcome with sorrow, which made him panic all the more, and in a rush he said: "We won't dissolve the contract!"

The words were out before he even knew what he had said — and before he could process his own statement, the figure in front of him shook with something else entirely, and a peal of laughter rang out and scattered across the courtyard.

Yuwen Luo turned away and hid his face in his hands.

The moment Lan Qi's laughter broke free, the entire courtyard came back to life as well, laughter breaking out from every corner — people smacking tables, throwing arms around each other's shoulders, pointing at Ning Lang, clutching their sides, dabbing at their eyes...

A joke. Of course it was a joke. What else could it be from the famously unrestrained Seventh Young Master of the Lan family!

The only person not laughing was Ning Lang. His face cycled through green, red, black, and white in rapid succession, and looking at Lan Qi laughing broadly ahead of him, at the whole courtyard of heroes doubled over with laughter around him, he could only think: this must be a dream. A nightmare.

And this "nightmare" was carried out of Longsky Manor by the jianghu heroes who had witnessed it, spread far and wide through the world of the jianghu, and became a source of mockery and amusement for quite a long time to come.

chapters.title: Chapter Five: Autumn River Waves, the Sky Itself Eclipsed (Part One)
chapters.content:
As the sun fell, the bustling Longsky Manor returned at last to quiet. The heroes from every direction had gone, and the four — Ming Huayan, Lan Canyin, Ning Lang, and Yuwen Luo — had been warmly pressed to stay by Qiu Changtian.

The bright moon rose early, flowers nodded half-open in the moonlight, and one by one the glass lanterns were lit and hung. In the Clear Wave Pavilion, Qiu Changtian set out a dinner table, sent servants to each courtyard to invite Ming, Lan, Ning, and Yuwen, and also called upon the already-visiting Nan Wofeng, Mei Hongming, and Hua Qinghe to join — the table was filled to a full and lively gathering.

Host and guests raised their cups, guests toasted the host, younger members toasted the elders — several rounds of pleasantries later, the mood around the table had grown warm and easy. "My worthy nephew" fell naturally from some lips; "Brother" and "Little Brother" flowed sincerely from others. Someone walking in who didn't know better might have thought it a family reunion.

"Brother Qinghe," Ming Er said, personally filling Hua Qinghe's cup, "before I left home, my father and mother repeatedly urged me to go to the Hua family in person to express our gratitude for your actions at Qiong City. My sixth younger sister was spared great harm thanks to your intervention — the entire Ming family is deeply grateful." He raised his cup in a gesture of respect. "Since we happen to meet here at Longsky Manor, I'll borrow these flowers to express our feelings — a toast to Brother Qinghe, a small token of our regard."

"You are too kind." Hua Qinghe quickly raised his cup in return.

Both drank and set down their cups.

"I hope the sixth miss's wound has fully healed?" Hua Qinghe inquired with genuine concern.

"Many thanks for Brother Qinghe's kind thought — Sixth Sister has completely recovered." Ming Er smiled with quiet refinement and looked at Hua Qinghe, something of deeper meaning just visible in his expression. "My sixth sister has always kept your life-saving grace in her heart, and has felt unable to repay it, which weighs on her. She has grown thin with the thought of it. If Brother Qinghe has time to spare, please do visit the Ming family — my father and mother would very much like a chance to properly thank you and set her mind at ease."

"The matter at Qiong City was simply what those of us in the jianghu ought to do. Uncle, Aunt, and the Sixth Miss need not think of it. I will certainly come to pay my respects when time allows." Hua Qinghe answered with easy grace.

"With Brother Qinghe's word, Ming Er is relieved." Ming Er gave a slight nod, then shifted his gaze to Mei Hongming, who had been sitting in quiet, absorbed thought. "Brother Hongming has been silent since the meal began. Could it be that the matter of the Lanyin Biyue weighs on your mind?"

Mei Hongming raised his head, and those refined eyes studied Ming Er for a moment before turning toward Lan Qi across the table. He said: "I was thinking about which hidden weapon of our Taoluo Gate could strike cleanly against the two of you."

"Hongming!" Nan Wofeng heard this and his expression tightened at once.

But Ming Er showed no displeasure at all, his smile remaining exactly as warm. "Senior Nan, the focus Brother Hongming brings to the study of martial arts is beyond what this junior could ever match. Taoluo Gate has a bright future ahead."

"How could my unworthy disciple compare to the Second Young Master." Nan Wofeng's face was properly stern, though his heart was in truth quite pleased.

"Not at all — I still have much to learn from the senior." Ming Er raised his clasped hands.

"Speaking of guidance — there is one matter this old man is actually quite concerned about, regarding the young master." Nan Wofeng stroked his white beard with the smile of a man who knows more than he lets on.

"What matter does the senior have in mind?" Ming Er asked with genuine humility.

"The Second Young Master is a dragon among men. But I wonder — has he yet found his companion dragon?" Nan Wofeng asked.

The question drew varied expressions from the table.

Lan Qi's jade fan "swish'd" open, and those jade-green eyes narrowed faintly.

Qiu Changtian smiled with warm and benevolent interest, watching Ming Er.

Hua Qinghe blinked, then continued smiling.

Mei Hongming looked at his master, then lowered his head again.

Yuwen Luo's eyes lit up.

Ning Lang looked at Lan Qi in bewilderment.

"This junior is one common mortal among many — how could I presume to hope for a phoenix from the sky?" Ming Er answered with a light, unhurried ease. He tilted his head slightly, those misty eyes drifting to the glass lantern on the wall, and continued: "This world holds no shortage of women of great beauty and varied charm. Yet what this junior hopes to find is simply someone willing to walk the road alongside him. Unfortunately fate has been thin — no such person has yet appeared." The last words carried the faintest shadow, a very quiet trace of regret.

Nan Wofeng and Qiu Changtian exchanged a glance — one stroked his beard and nodded, the other smiled and nodded as well.

"If this old man had a daughter, I would seek to make the Second Young Master her husband too." Nan Wofeng said with playful warmth, and then turned to look at Qiu Changtian: "Speaking of daughters, Long Tian — where is Hengbo? We have so many fine young heroes here this evening, and they are all close in age — she ought to come out and get to know everyone. You should have her join us."

Qiu Changtian gave a start, then slapped his forehead: "How did I forget — Qiu Zang, go and invite the young miss to come."

"Yes."

The young men at the table, hearing that Qiu Hengbo — one of the two great beauties of the martial world — was soon to appear, could not help showing their pleasure. "Autumn river waves, a loveliness past compare" — what manner of beauty could those words describe?

"The layout of the courtyard today was all clever conception and skilled execution — I heard it was entirely of Miss Qiu's design. It seems Miss Qiu is not only peerlessly beautiful but of exceptional intelligence and taste as well." Lan Qi swayed his jade fan lightly.

"You flatter her, Seventh Young Master." Qiu Changtian beamed. "My daughter just happened to read a few stray books — the manor's layout was mostly done by her following whatever she read in those books. It's quite rough, really. You are all too kind." He paused with a smile. "I hear she is not yet spoken for. One wonders who will be so fortunate one day." He said this and glanced meaningfully at Ming Er.

"Ha ha..." Qiu Changtian laughed warmly. "Hengbo has always had a strong sense of herself. So in this matter of her life's companion, I respect her wishes — so long as she is satisfied with the choice, I have no objection." His own gaze also landed on Ming Er.

In the middle of this conversation, a light, quick set of footsteps sounded from somewhere nearby, followed by the drift of a faint, clean fragrance. Then a slender, pale-blue silhouette stepped through the door — and in that instant, the bright glass lanterns of the pavilion seemed to soften into a shimmer of water, the whole room blurring into a gentle, wavering light. The glass lanterns swayed like soft ripples. That pale-blue silhouette seemed to step lightly across those ripples as she came forward.

"Hengbo, come here." Qiu Changtian called.

"Father. Senior Nan." Qiu Hengbo moved with the grace of lotus steps.

"Hengbo — your father will introduce you to a few young heroes. This is the Second Young Master of the Ming family, Ming Huayan. This is the Seventh Young Master of the Lan family, Lan Canyin. This is the eldest son of the Hua family, Hua Qinghe. This is Mei Hongming of Taoluo Gate. This is Yuwen Luo of the Yuwen family. And this is Ning Lang of the Ning family." Qiu Changtian introduced each in turn.

Qiu Hengbo raised her eyes to look at each person at the table, meeting six pairs of eyes — each different in character, each equally struck. She was neither embarrassed nor shy, but composed and natural. She bowed with graceful ease. "Hengbo greets each of the young masters."

The men rose one after another to return the greeting.

Qiu Hengbo's gaze moved slowly across the faces at the table. They were indeed as her father had said — young heroes, and remarkably so: refined bearing, distinguished air, none of the coarseness of common people. The two who stood out most were undeniably the Second Young Master of the Ming family and the Seventh Young Master of the Lan family — and yet, somehow, when her gaze met Lan Qi's jade-green eyes without warning, her heart gave a small lurch. A faint chill passed through her. And yet, as she looked at him, she could also feel clearly — this man known as the "Jade Demon" held no ill intent toward her whatsoever. In those eyes that could bewitch the heart was a true appreciation of her — and a smile of faint, puzzling amusement.

"Hengbo — the Celestial Silk Robe you wove with your own hands did not find its recipient today." Qiu Changtian looked at his daughter with a meaningful expression. "First, the matter of the Lanyin Biyue's theft interrupted things. And second, the bout between Huayan and the Seventh Young Master ended without a clear winner."

One was "Huayan, my worthy nephew." The other was simply "the Seventh Young Master." The difference in affection was plain. Yuwen Luo smiled privately to himself, then turned to look at Ning Lang — whose eyes were fixed on Lan Qi and had been since the table was set — with a mix of amusement and sympathy. His gaze shifted to Lan Qi: from top to bottom, then back from bottom to top, a careful and thorough inspection. That face — truly too... well, "too" was the only word. One couldn't use that word to describe a man, but truly, what other word was there? His eyes lingered at the collar. Unfortunately, the neckline covered everything. Even so, looking at those brows and eyes, that manner and bearing, every word and gesture was purely, unmistakably male — this could not be a woman in disguise.

"Hengbo was not present today, but she heard the story from the manor's people. A few moves between the Second Young Master and the Seventh Young Master, and the entire gathering was said to have been stunned." Qiu Hengbo stepped closer to the table and with her own hands filled the cups of Ming Er and Lan Qi, then poured one for herself as well. She raised her cup. "The highest skill finds no equal — yet before it, solitude. Hengbo congratulates both of you on having found each other as rivals."

The remark landed unexpectedly. Lan Qi and Ming Er both let a glimmer of surprise into their eyes. They looked at Qiu Hengbo for a moment — then rose together, cups held high, and drank.

Ming Er set down his cup, his gaze resting on Qiu Hengbo. "'Autumn river waves, a loveliness past compare' seems to have gotten it wrong."

This made everyone at the table blink in surprise. How could that be wrong? In their eyes, the phrase still fell short of capturing her beauty.

"It should be: 'Autumn river waves, the sky itself eclipsed; eyes bright with wisdom, heart fine as jade, outshining the constellations.'" Ming Er recited softly.

Qiu Hengbo felt something stir in her heart. The eyes she had been so carefully keeping averted finally turned toward Ming Er, and the moment she met those eyes veiled in their gentle mist, it was as though a hundred lives rushed by — morning after morning and evening after evening, year after year, she had always been waiting for these eyes, but they always seemed just beyond reach, glimpsed across mountains and across rivers.

"Mm — very well said indeed. Hengbo has earned these words." Nan Wofeng stroked his beard with warm approval. He looked at Ming Er, then at Qiu Hengbo. A truly matched pair, fit for the jade terrace and the immortal realm.

"Quite so." Those at the table nodded in agreement.

Qiu Hengbo smiled faintly, and a wave of radiance moved through those bright autumn-water eyes — every kind of beauty and every kind of grace alive within them. Every man present gave a secret sigh of admiration: "Autumn river waves, a loveliness past compare" — absolutely deserved.

"I have long heard that the Second Young Master excels in calligraphy. I wonder if it would be too much to ask for a piece of your writing?" Qiu Hengbo's bright clear eyes looked directly at Ming Er.

A slight pause around the table at this — but only Lan Qi curved his lips and smiled to himself. He turned his head idly, and his gaze landed straight on Ning Lang's — who promptly went scarlet to the ears.

Qiu Changtian looked at his daughter and understood at once. He exchanged a glance with Nan Wofeng, and both smiled in quiet satisfaction.

"If the young miss does not think too poorly of my work, I would be glad to." Ming Er smiled in acceptance.

"Qiu Zang — have paper and ink prepared." Qiu Changtian at once gave the instruction.

In a short while, a writing desk had been carried in, paper laid, ink ground.

Ming Er rose from his seat and came to the desk, dipped his brush, then asked: "What words would the young miss like?"

"Whatever comes to the Second Young Master's heart." Qiu Hengbo moved the paperweight to hold down the white paper.

Ming Er's gaze shifted from the paper to Qiu Hengbo herself — here was rare beauty, matched with rare intelligence, and rare grace of character. What more could anyone ask?

The brush came down. In an instant, dragons and phoenixes took flight across the paper.

On the other side, Lan Qi looked at the writing and read aloud, without thinking: "To the west there is a beauty, radiant as the morning sun. In silk and fine brocade she walks, with jade ornaments at her side. Her grace adorns her beauty, and in the soft breeze, she shines. She climbs the height and looks toward longing, and lifts her sleeve toward the morning light. Her spirit rises to the heavens between the clouds, her sleeve floats free above the void..."

Only Ning Lang sat distracted, his eyes trailing after Lan Qi without purpose. Yuwen Luo was beside him.

"Stop looking — no matter how long you look, he is still a man." Yuwen Luo saw where Ning Lang's eyes kept going, and sighed.

"I know." Ning Lang bowed his head in misery.

"How is your family involved in all this — how does your family come to have a marriage contract with a man?" Yuwen Luo asked.

"I don't know." Ning Lang raised his head, those round eyes full of puzzlement and trouble. "I lived on Qianbei Mountain the whole time, and only came down this year. I was barely home for a month before Mother told me she had made a match for me when I was small — to someone from the Lan family of Yun Province named Lan Canyin. She told me to go to the Lan family and bring my bride home."

Pfft. Yuwen Luo couldn't help but laugh. He fixed his gaze on Ning Lang's still somewhat boyish face. "Bring your bride home? In that state of yours — going to bring a bride home?"

Being laughed at on top of his misery only made Ning Lang more agitated. "That's what Mother said."

"So what are you going to do about it now?" Yuwen Luo pointed at Lan Qi. "That's a man."

"I don't know." Ning Lang was troubled. "Big Brother — if it were you, what would you do?"

"Me?" Yuwen Luo pointed at himself, then made a grand, sweeping gesture. "Dissolve the contract, obviously."

"But earlier..." Ning Lang thought of the sorrowful look on Lan Qi's face and hesitated.

"Idiot!" Yuwen Luo flicked a finger against the top of his head. "He was playing you. And you fell for it."

chapters.title: Chapter Five: Autumn River Waves, the Sky Itself Eclipsed (Part Two)
chapters.content:
"Playing me?" Ning Lang's face went pale, then an instant later flooded red. "He...he actually used something like that to play games with me!"

"Who told you to be so simple-minded!" Yuwen Luo rolled his eyes. "Obviously, two men cannot get married — he knows that perfectly well. And besides, his romantic exploits have traveled from one end of the jianghu to the other — he is clearly not someone with a taste for that kind of thing. He had already accomplished his purpose earlier today — the whole thing was a bit of theater, and everyone else took it as such. But behind that theater, there was a message: namely, that the two great families, the Lan family and the Ning family, share an unusually deep bond. After all, having gotten to the point of discussing marriage, the connection must be one of deep feeling and long trust. Not to mention — who in the jianghu doesn't know that the Ning family and Qianbei Mountain are cut from the same cloth? A deep tie with the Ning family is naturally a deep tie with Qianbei Mountain as well."

"Oh." Ning Lang rubbed his eyes, feeling a little drowsy.

"Lan Qi — that man thinks swiftly and acts decisively. He is exceptionally formidable." Yuwen Luo turned his teacup in his fingers. "And that Second Young Master, Ming Huayan, defeats his enemies without them even knowing."

Ning Lang yawned, and asked: "How so?"

Yuwen Luo took a sip of tea before answering: "At the table, he brought up the story of the eldest Hua son saving the Ming family's sixth young miss — on the surface, he was saying the Ming family is grateful. Underneath, he was revealing that the sixth young miss has feelings for Hua Qinghe, and that the Ming family's parents look on him favorably. Qiu Changtian — a man of his perceptiveness — heard the subtext clearly and would of course never compete for someone already marked by the Ming family. And looking at Hua Qinghe's reaction when he asked after the sixth young miss, you could see there was likely some feeling there too — which means Qiu Changtian would be even less inclined to consider him for his daughter. Then there is Mei Hongming — that one remark of his showed genuine, open-hearted single-mindedness, but also made clear that he has no feeling for the ways of people and the world around him. He may achieve great things on the martial path one day, but he is not the kind of person who could command the heroes of the jianghu as their sovereign. Qiu Changtian is known as the Scholar Hero — a man of broad talent and wide acquaintance, at ease in every world. Someone of his nature would naturally be drawn to Ming Er, who is most like him."

"Oh." Ning Lang gave another long yawn, thinking of nothing but bed.

"And then Qiu Hengbo arrived, and that beauty — what man could remain unmoved? And so came the writing, and the robe, and though no words were spoken outright, every person at the table understood: those were the tokens of a betrothal. And Lan Qi — not willing to let them have it too easily — casually mentions his ninth younger sister, planting a thorn in Qiu Hengbo's heart: a man of Ming Er's caliber is one that every woman would want — and men taking two, three, four wives is, after all, entirely normal... ha ha... killing his enemies with a smile..." Yuwen Luo chuckled to himself, his eyes alive with delight. "It really is all so interesting — there are this many remarkable and interesting people in the world, and it all happens at once with the Lanyin Biyue going missing and the jianghu beginning to stir again. Heaven surely had some grand purpose in mind when it created me — to witness this moment in history!" With these words, his face filled with such confidence and excitement that he might genuinely have believed himself chosen by fate.

But Ning Lang had long since stopped caring about Yuwen Luo's excitement. He was exhausted, and he was getting up to head for bed. "Big Brother, it's very late — sleep. We can talk tomorrow."

"Hey — did you actually hear any of what I just said?" Yuwen Luo rose and followed, demanding to know.

"Yes, I heard it — isn't it just saying that the Second Young Master Ming and the Seventh Young Master Lan are evenly matched rivals? The young miss Qiu already said that herself." Ning Lang gave a dismissive wave and climbed onto the bed.

"Hey — it's not that simple." Yuwen Luo grabbed his arm. "Ming Er and Lan Qi — those two men, I can't read them. One is out-of-this-world but still moves through the mortal one; the other walks in the moral world but carries an air of the unearthly. You need to be careful from here on out — especially that Lan Qi."

"Mm." Ning Lang's eyes were already half shut. He turned over without further ceremony, and shortly the sound of steady, even breathing told the room he was already asleep.

"Hey!" Yuwen Luo pushed at him and got nothing. "Fine, I'll sleep too." He pushed Ning Lang further toward the wall, lay down, pulled the blanket over himself, and in a little while he too had drifted off.

The next morning, both of them slept late. Outside, the sun was already high.

"Did you both sleep well?" Qiu Changtian asked with a warm smile. "Last night everyone had a few cups too many, so I had the servants leave you undisturbed. I let you sleep in."

Yuwen Luo and Ning Lang walked in to find everyone already seated at the table — they were the only two late arrivals, faces flushing simultaneously with embarrassment.

"We overslept — please forgive us for making everyone wait." Yuwen Luo and Ning Lang apologized together.

"Never mind — come sit down and eat." Qiu Changtian waved them over.

"Did Young Brother Ning have pleasant dreams last night?"

Ning Lang had just been about to sit when Lan Qi's question suddenly reached his ears. Something lurched in his chest, and before he could steady himself he had sat down too hard — bang — and the perfectly sturdy chair gave way beneath him, scattering into pieces. He landed on the ground.

The table stared for one stunned moment — then Lan Qi was the first to laugh out loud, and Hua Qinghe and Mei Hongming followed close behind. Even Qiu Changtian and Nan Wofeng were unable to suppress their amusement. Even Ming Er's face broke into a smile. Everyone looked at Ning Lang on the ground with a mixture of sympathy and helpless laughter. Yuwen Luo's expression was caught precisely between wanting to laugh and wanting to cry.

"Qiu Zang — have someone bring a replacement chair at once." Qiu Changtian gave the order quickly, then looked with concern toward Ning Lang. "Are you hurt, Worthy Nephew?"

"Not at all, not at all." Ning Lang sprang to his feet, took one look at Lan Qi, who was still laughing, and felt something sink quietly in his chest. He turned away.

"How clumsy of me — I gave you a start." Lan Qi composed himself and offered a formal bow. "I hope Young Brother will pardon the oversight."
